items.headline: Update: NEA issues haze notices to seven named Indonesian firms
items.summary: On 16 October, Environment Minister Grace Fu said the NEA is issuing preventive-measure notices under the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act to seven Indonesian companies identified as sources of this month's haze.

items.headline: Ex-inmate from CNA prison documentary jailed again for reoffending
items.summary: Graceson Ang, who appeared in CNA's 'Inside Maximum Security', was sentenced to three years and one month plus 510 extra days after pleading guilty to six charges.

items.headline: Chain collision of three buses in Yishun injures five
items.summary: A Tower Transit Service 853 bus rear-ended a Service 852 bus at Yishun Avenue 2 on 15 October, triggering a chain collision; five people were taken to hospital and no drivers were hurt.

items.headline: Bukit Panjang LRT renewal substantially completed after eight years
items.summary: The LTA said the eight-year Bukit Panjang LRT renewal is substantially complete, with the vehicle fleet, signalling and control-centre upgrades done and lift upgrades at 11 of 13 stations by end-October.

items.headline: Singapore-bound SIA flight returns to San Francisco after unruly passenger
items.summary: Singapore Airlines flight SQ31 turned back to San Francisco after a passenger became unruly and injured himself; the A350 later re-departed for Singapore with a fresh crew.

items.headline: Update: Foreign investors pull a record US$32.5bn from Indian stocks in 2026
items.summary: Foreign portfolio investors have sold about US$32.5 billion of Indian shares in 2026 — a record — after 13 straight selling sessions, with the rupee near its all-time low of about 96.97 per dollar.

items.headline: US Secretary of State Rubio to visit Reliance's Jamnagar refinery
items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is set to visit Reliance Industries' Jamnagar refinery, which processes about 1.4 million barrels of crude a day, as US diesel prices climb.

items.headline: Ex-DUP leader Jeffrey Donaldson jailed for 15 years for child sex offences
items.summary: Jeffrey Donaldson, 63, the former DUP leader, was sentenced at Newry Crown Court to 15 years for one rape and multiple indecent assaults against children between 1985 and 2008; he is appealing.

items.headline: Chancellor Healey backs a third Heathrow runway, risking a clash with PM Burnham
items.summary: Chancellor John Healey publicly backed a third Heathrow runway as a pro-growth measure, Bloomberg reported, setting up a potential split with PM Andy Burnham.

items.headline: Bank of England's Bailey sees little sign of entrenched inflation
items.summary: BoE Governor Andrew Bailey said there is little evidence of inflation becoming embedded in UK wage- and price-setting; the Bank held Bank Rate at 3.75% in September and the Budget is due 28 October.

items.headline: Harry and Meghan make first joint UK public engagement since returning
items.summary: The Duke and Duchess of Sussex visited a charity in Nottingham on 15 October in their first joint public appearance in Britain since relocating back; CNN noted it was not an official royal engagement.

items.headline: Russell Brand branded a 'ruthless predator' as his sex-assault trial opens
items.summary: Prosecutors told Southwark Crown Court that Russell Brand acted as a 'ruthless' sexual predator against six women between 1999 and 2009; Brand denies the charges and the trial is continuing.

items.headline: EU leaders rally behind Ukraine as the Trump-Zelensky rift widens
items.summary: At a European Council in Brussels, EU leaders pressed to keep arming Ukraine as Washington-Kyiv ties soured; the summit ended with no budget deal and a 70-billion-euro Ukraine funding gap unresolved.

items.headline: Seven sailors missing after drone strikes hit two tankers off Romania
items.summary: Two chemical tankers caught fire off Romania after drone strikes on 15 October; seven crew of the Wine Trader are missing. President Nicusor Dan said two drones hit the ships and a NATO source blamed Russia.

items.headline: Ethiopia installs a six-month interim administration in Tigray
items.summary: PM Abiy Ahmed announced a federally directed caretaker administration to govern Tigray for six months and prepare elections, after forces repelled a TPLF offensive and retook Mekelle.

items.headline: Settlers attack Palestinian olive harvesters and a US journalist in the West Bank
items.summary: About 80 Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian olive harvesters at Abu Falah on 16 October; Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine was beaten and about ten Palestinians were wounded.

items.headline: Pakistan-Afghanistan tensions persist after Moscow talks end without a deal
items.summary: Border tensions between Pakistan and Afghanistan continued after Moscow-format consultations ended with no joint statement; Islamabad ties dialogue to action on cross-border militancy, which the Taliban reject.

items.headline: Anthropic gives METR evaluators employee-level access to probe its AI models
items.summary: Anthropic granted six researchers from nonprofit evaluator METR employee-level access and gave up the right to block METR from publishing its own assessments, keeping only narrow redaction rights.

items.headline: China proposes export controls on its own advanced AI models and chips
items.summary: China proposed adding 23 AI technologies to its export-control catalogue, covering the largest models' weights and chip designs at 14nm and below; a registration rule took effect 16 October, Bloomberg reported.

items.headline: Taiwan to fund up to US$4bn Texas complex for AI-hardware suppliers
items.summary: Taiwan will back US industrial parks for AI-hardware suppliers, the first a Texas complex costing up to US$4 billion, minister Kung Ming-hsin said; no commitments yet from Nvidia or TSMC, Bloomberg reported.

items.headline: Google launches Universal Cart shopping across Search and Gemini in the US
items.summary: Google rolled out Universal Cart in the US across Search and the Gemini app, with one cart across retailers, price-drop alerts and in-cart checkout; launch merchants include Nike, Target and Walmart.

items.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang says the AI-stock selloff 'is going to pass'
items.summary: In Berlin, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang played down the slide in AI and chip stocks, saying 'all of this is going to pass', Bloomberg reported, as semiconductor shares logged a long losing streak.

items.headline: Nasdaq falls 2.1% on Friday for its worst week since June
items.summary: The Nasdaq fell 2.1% and the S&P 500 lost 1.1% on 16 October on AI-debt and chip fears, their worst week since June; a semiconductor index fell 3.8% for an eighth straight down day.

items.headline: Jakarta stocks crash about 12% in their worst day since 1998
items.summary: Indonesia's Jakarta Composite plunged roughly 12% on 16 October — its biggest one-day fall since 1998 — after MSCI opened a consultation on cutting it to 'standalone' status; Goldman saw up to US$13bn of outflows.

items.headline: Fed's Warsh gives no October steer, cementing bets on a rate hold
items.summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh declined to signal the October decision at IMF meetings, Bloomberg reported, leaving markets pricing a roughly 82% chance of a hold at 3.75%-4% on 27-28 October.

items.headline: Thoma Bravo's Proofpoint to buy Varonis for US$6.3bn
items.summary: Proofpoint, owned by Thoma Bravo, agreed to buy data-security firm Varonis for about US$6.3 billion at US$49.75 a share, with Ontario Teachers' co-investing; close expected in H1 2027, Bloomberg reported.

items.headline: Citizens Financial third-quarter profit jumps 29% to US$636m
items.summary: Citizens Financial Group reported Q3 net income of US$636 million, up 29% year on year, with EPS of US$1.41, and raised its dividend by 13%.

items.headline: Medvedev beats Tommy Paul to reach the Shanghai Masters semi-finals
items.summary: Former champion Daniil Medvedev beat Tommy Paul 6-3, 1-6, 6-3 on 16 October to reach the Shanghai Masters semi-finals, where he meets Rafael Jodar.

items.headline: Jodar becomes the youngest Shanghai Masters semi-finalist
items.summary: Spain's Rafael Jodar, 20, beat Casper Ruud 4-6, 6-4, 6-3 on 16 October to become the youngest semi-finalist in Shanghai Masters history.

items.headline: Antonelli can clinch the 2026 F1 title at the US Grand Prix
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli leads the drivers' championship on 340 points, 102 clear of George Russell, heading into the US Grand Prix in Austin (23-25 October), where he could seal his first title.

items.headline: India and West Indies meet in a Bengaluru decider with the T20I series level
items.summary: The five-match T20I series is tied 2-2 ahead of the decider at Bengaluru on 17 October; India added Bhuvneshwar Kumar, with Arshdeep Singh a doubt and Jasprit Bumrah rested.

items.headline: World's timekeepers vote to abolish the leap second
items.summary: At the General Conference on Weights and Measures in Versailles on 15 October, member states voted to scrap the leap second and replace it with a far rarer 'leap hour'.

items.headline: Scientists propose how microplastics may trigger inflammation
items.summary: A study reported by Scientific American suggests water near a microplastic's surface can generate reactive oxygen species, a possible mechanism for microplastic-linked inflammation.

items.headline: ESA's Hera probe fires a 93-minute burn as it nears asteroid Dimorphos
items.summary: ESA's Hera spacecraft carried out a 93-minute braking burn on 15 October to slow toward the Didymos-Dimorphos asteroid, which it will survey after NASA's 2022 DART impact.

items.headline: Study links a brain enzyme to memory resilience in old age
items.summary: Research reported in Nature ties an enzyme encoded by the gene Pla2g2f to cognitive resilience; aged mice lacking it showed more brain inflammation, while extra copies improved spatial memory.

items.headline: Scientists turn cloned male mouse embryos into fertile females with CRISPR
items.summary: Researchers used a CRISPR tool called Y-CUT to remove the Y chromosome from male mouse embryos, producing fertile XO females, Scientific American reported, as a possible aid to saving endangered species.

fun_fact.headline: Bamboo is the fastest-growing plant on Earth
fun_fact.body: Bamboo is the fastest-growing plant on Earth. Some species can shoot up by as much as 91 cm (about 35 inches) in a single day — fast enough that, in the right conditions, you could almost watch it rise. The spurt comes from cells stretching between the stem's nodes, powered by energy stored in the plant's underground rhizomes.
fun_fact.source: Guinness World Records; BBC Discover Wildlife

puzzle.title: The Spider and the Fly
puzzle.body:
A rectangular room is 30 ft long, 12 ft wide and 12 ft high.

A spider sits at the middle of one end wall, 1 ft below the ceiling. A fly rests at the middle of the opposite end wall, 1 ft above the floor (in line with the spider, 30 ft away).

The spider can only crawl along the surfaces — walls, floor and ceiling. What is the length of the shortest path it can take to reach the fly?
puzzle.approach: Don't trust the obvious route over the walls. The shortest path across a solid can be found by 'unfolding' the faces flat and drawing a straight line.
puzzle.answer:
40 feet.

The tempting route — 1 ft up to the ceiling, 30 ft across it, then 11 ft down the far wall — measures 42 ft. But a shorter path exists that crosses five of the room's six faces.

Unfold those faces into one flat plane and the spider-to-fly path becomes a straight line. Its two legs work out to 32 ft (1 + 30 + 1) and 24 ft (6 + 12 + 6), so the distance is the square root of (32 squared + 24 squared) = square root of (1024 + 576) = square root of 1600 = 40 ft.

A classic puzzle devised by Henry Dudeney.

word_puzzle.title: Hive Mind
word_puzzle.body:
Centre letter:  T   (every word must use it)
Outer letters:  A  C  E  N  O  R

Rules: words of 4+ letters; letters may be reused; no proper nouns.

Goal: find the pangram that uses all seven letters, plus as many other words as you can.
word_puzzle.approach: Build as many words of four or more letters as you can, using only the seven letters shown. Every word must contain the centre letter, and letters may be reused. One word — the pangram — uses all seven.
word_puzzle.answer:
Pangram: CAROTENE — it uses all seven letters (T, A, C, E, N, O, R).

A sample of valid words (each contains T and uses only A/C/E/N/O/R/T):
RATE · CART · CRATE · TRACE · REACT · CATER · CRATER · TRACER · NECTAR · CANTER · RECANT · TRANCE · OCTANE · CARTON · TENOR · TONER · ATONE · ORNATE · REACTOR · CREATOR · TERRACE · CONCERT · CONTRACT

Many more are possible — anything of four or more letters built only from these seven and containing T.
